items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Dallas Bartley's band I think he played with

ctx.x: down in a train station... Billy Eckstine would tell him, "We need an arrangement on so-and-so-and-so," and if we had a couple of hours to wait in the train station, he would sit down, and by that night, when we got to where we were going, he would have the arrangement. If we didn't play it on the bandstand that night, we'd rehearse it the next day. Sometimes he did it with a score, Other times he didn't use a score.

But I just couldn't... I never have been able to understand how he could do this, and come up with good arrangements, and no piano, nothing. He was a trombone player. Although he did play piano. He could play the piano, and he knew the piano well. But he only used it for arranging. A couple of times I heard him play a few things. As a matter of fact, I think he played piano with a group in Chicago, a small group, Dallas Bartley's band I think he played with, a guy that was formerly with Louis Jordan.

But to get back to the band. Jerry Valentine was a trombone player. And there was another r young fellow there, we used to call him Scotty -- I can't remember what his first name was. I think his last name was Scott, which is the reason why they called him Scotty.
